gbm_population_evidence.quote: Patient previously diagnosed with WHO grade 4 IDH-wildtype GBM

candidate_evidence.quote: will be administered pembrolizumab along with focused ultrasound sonication following surgery for recurrent glioblastoma

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Pilot Study of Navigated Focused Ultrasound and Pembrolizumab in the Treatment of Recurrent WHO Grade 4 IDH-Wildtype Glioblastoma With Mismatch Repair Deficiency

role_evidence.quote: Treatment dosing will be 200mg of pembrolizumab every three weeks for up to six months or until disease progression, whichever occurs first.
following microbubble (Bracco Imaging, SonoVue® or Lumason®; 0.1 mL/Kg; maximum 4.8 mL) administration on a 2-minute schedule

agents.drug_class_hint: ultrasound contrast microbubbles used with focused ultrasound sonication

source_quote.quote: MMR deficiencies confirmed per standard of care immunohistochemical analysis or Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) of the patient's surgical sample from the time of initial GBM diagnosis or recurrence.
Patient previously diagnosed with WHO grade 4 IDH-wildtype GBM
To evaluate levels of baseline tumor markers related to immune and genetic repair function, including PD-L1, microsatellite instability (MSI), and tumor mutational burden (TMB).

coder_notes: Pembrolizumab is paired with NaviFUS focused ultrasound sonication after microbubble administration, so device_dependent is true per R4; the record does not state that the device is needed for the antitumour effect. Microbubbles listed as delivery-enabling because they are used for the focused ultrasound procedure (BBB opening not explicitly stated). Regimen is monotherapy: no other antitumour drug or radiotherapy in the experimental arm. Single-arm; allocation NA. The second TMB_MMR row covers the MSI and TMB baseline marker outcome.
